summary: Lisa Park and Rachel Torres met with Philip Lau and CISO Danielle Ortiz of Keystone Health, who confirmed their decision to add Aegis Detect to their existing Comply and Protect contract. Danielle said she had serious reservations after the March outage, but the candid game day summary, which included the failed network partition test, built credibility. Philip cited tool consolidation and Comply v2 saving around 60 hours on the last HIPAA cycle, with Detect evidence flowing into Comply as a single audit trail. Lisa confirmed Detect will co-term with the existing three-year agreement and include the enhanced 99.9% SLA and the June pipeline health panel. Danielle asked for early access to heartbeat alerts and offered to be a reference customer, and onboarding is targeted for the week of June 8.
actionItems: Lisa Park: Send the revised order form and updated Detect security questionnaire by Friday
Rachel Torres: Check whether Keystone can receive heartbeat alerts before the pipeline health panel ships in June
Rachel Torres: Schedule the Detect onboarding kickoff for the week of June 8
